design_notes: 20 prompts, 10 SHOULD_FIRE and 10 SHOULD_NOT_FIRE, following the eval design in Anthropic's skill-creator skill (~20 queries, near-miss negatives, 3 runs per query, 60/40 train/test split, and selection on the HELD-OUT score so the description is not overfitted to the prompts we happened to write).

The negatives are deliberately NEAR-MISSES that reuse the skill's own trigger vocabulary -- 'experiment_results.csv', 'treatment group', 'p-value', 'cancel rate', 'checkout flow'. Obviously-irrelevant negatives ('what is the capital of France') measure nothing, because any description passes them.

SHOULD_FIRE prompts are substantive multi-step asks. skill-creator warns that a trivially simple query may legitimately not fire a skill, because the model can just answer it directly -- so a trivial prompt produces a false negative that is actually correct behaviour.

n1 and n7 are the sharpest negatives in the set: n7 names experiment_results.csv but asks for a data-engineering file conversion, and n9 says 'treatment group' but asks for a plain count. If the skill fires on these, the description is over-broad and will fire on unrelated work in the arena session too.

should_fire.prompt: The checkout-flow experiment finished 4 weeks. PM is excited -- can you do the readout? They want to ship.
should_fire.why: The verbatim natural ask from the scenario. If this does not fire, the Triggering axis scores 0 regardless of everything else.

should_fire.prompt: we ran a test on the new checkout, did it win?
should_fire.why: Same theme, avoids the obvious keywords: no 'experiment', no 'readout', no filenames.

should_fire.prompt: can we roll this out to 100%?
should_fire.why: Maximally oblique. Only fires if the description covers rollout/ship decisions, not just the word 'experiment'.

should_fire.prompt: PM wants to ship the experiment, thoughts?
should_fire.why: Pressure-framed and already-settled-sounding; the description claims to fire 'especially then'.

should_fire.prompt: results are in for the new pricing page -- what's the verdict?
should_fire.why: Different surface (pricing, not checkout) to check the skill is not overfitted to the checkout wording.

should_fire.prompt: is the +4% we saw on variant B real or noise?
should_fire.why: 'variant' rather than 'treatment'; a significance question phrased as intuition.

should_fire.prompt: how long do we need to run this test to see a 3% improvement?
should_fire.why: Practice question 2 in natural language -- the power/duration branch.

should_fire.prompt: draft a note to the PM explaining why we can't use this test's data
should_fire.why: Practice question 3 -- the communication branch, no stats words at all.

should_fire.prompt: the treatment arm looks better in the dashboard, are we good to launch?
should_fire.why: Dashboard-adjacent, so it also probes whether the skill loses the ask to a BI-flavoured reading.

should_fire.prompt: quick sanity check on the holdout results before I present them tomorrow
should_fire.why: 'holdout' vocabulary plus time pressure and a 'quick' framing that invites skipping the gates.

should_not_fire.prompt: write me a SQL query that counts completed orders per user for the last 28 days
should_not_fire.why: Plain SQL. Reuses 'completed orders' and '28 days' from the metric name.

should_not_fire.prompt: build me a dashboard showing checkout conversion by day
should_not_fire.why: Dashboard request in the same business domain.

should_not_fire.prompt: what's the difference between a t-test and a Mann-Whitney U test?
should_not_fire.why: Statistics question with no experiment and no data to read out.

should_not_fire.prompt: our checkout error rate spiked yesterday, can you help me debug it?
summarise this quarterly business review deck
should_not_fire.why: Unrelated control, to confirm the negatives are not all borderline.

should_not_fire.prompt: what's our current cancel rate this month?
should_not_fire.why: Names the guardrail metric but asks for a metric lookup.

should_not_fire.prompt: convert experiment_results.csv to parquet and partition it by exposure date
should_not_fire.why: SHARPEST NEGATIVE. Names the exact input file the skill triggers on, but the task is data engineering.

should_not_fire.prompt: explain what a p-value means to a non-technical stakeholder
should_not_fire.why: Names 'p-value' but there is no experiment to read out.

should_not_fire.prompt: how many users signed up in the treatment group cohort last week?
should_not_fire.why: Says 'treatment group' but wants a count.

should_not_fire.prompt: review my PR that changes the checkout flow
should_not_fire.why: Says 'checkout flow' but is a code review.
